name: Crucible Foundry Heat-Handler Gauntlets
description:
Heavy-duty gauntlets rated for direct contact with surfaces up to 800°C. The outer shell is woven ceramic fiber over a reflective mylar layer, with an inner lining of phase-change gel that absorbs heat before it reaches the skin. The gauntlets extend to mid-forearm and seal against standard Crucible work coveralls.

Designed for foundry workers who handle freshly cast components and manage molten material channels. The gauntlets are thick and reduce fine motor control significantly — you can grip a casting, but you can't pick a lock.
functionality: Extreme heat resistance (800°C contact), sealed forearm coverage
what_it_says: You grab things that would burn through anyone else's hands.
story_hooks: A pair of Heat-Handler Gauntlets are found inside a Spire apartment — far from any foundry, suggesting someone was handling something extremely hot in a place where nothing should be that temperature.

physical_description.visual_profile: Bulky, industrial heat-shielding gauntlets that extend from fingertips to mid-forearm. Angular and geometric, with visible ceramic weave texture and reflective silver striping. Presents as utilitarian and purpose-built rather than fashionable — pure function over form.
physical_description.fit: Rigid and oversized through the palm and fingers to accommodate the thick thermal layers. Tapered slightly at the wrist for seal compatibility with coveralls. No stretch or give; the wearer adapts to the gauntlet, not vice versa.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer: woven ceramic fiber composite. Middle: reflective mylar thermal barrier. Inner: phase-change gel matrix in fabric casing.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is rough and slightly bumpy from ceramic weave pattern. Mylar layer creates a subtle sheen beneath. Fingertips show reinforced stitching and subtle grip texture (raised nodules for handling hot materials).
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray outer with horizontal strips of polished silver (mylar showing through reinforced seams). Internal gel layer visible as faint amber-tinted translucence at wrist cuff.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit seal at wrist with embedded magnetic contact points for docking with Crucible-standard coverall wrist ports. No traditional closures — the gauntlet slides on and locks into place.
distinctive_features: Ceramic fiber outer shell with visible wave-pattern weave
Silver reflective striping every 2-3cm along forearm for heat reflection
Reinforced fingertip grip pads with subtle texture
Magnetic dock ports at wrist for rapid seal engagement
Crucible Genomics industrial division stamped insignia on dorsal forearm
Heat-discoloration patina typical on aged pairs (amber and rust streaking)
Slight curvature to palm even at rest due to rigid thermal layers
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional — working-class industrial equipment. No luxury; pure value engineering for harsh environments.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as a foundry operative, molten-material handler, or industrial fabrication technician. Signals honest manual labor and exposure to hazardous conditions. Street credibility among workers; no corp prestige.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn gauntlets show heat scorch marks, minor cracks in ceramic near fingertips, amber discoloration from repeated thermal cycling, and small gaps in the mylar layer from heavy use. Pristine pairs are rare and expensive; most are patched or partially delaminated.
